name: Fahad al-Thumairy

summary.text: Fahad al-Thumairy was an accredited Saudi diplomat at the Saudi consulate in Los Angeles and an imam at the King Fahad Mosque in Culver City, California, employed by Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Islamic Affairs. The 9/11 Commission (2004) examined whether he helped hijackers Nawaf al-Hazmi and Khalid al-Mihdhar after they arrived in Los Angeles in January 2000 and reported that it had not found evidence that he did. He was refused entry to the United States in May 2003. He was one of the three main subjects of the FBI's Operation Encore investigation, whose closing material, released under Executive Order 14040, states that the evidence did not establish that he, Omar al-Bayoumi and Musaed al-Jarrah knowingly conspired to assist the hijackers. He has never been charged and has denied helping the hijackers. The 9/11 families' lawsuit against Saudi Arabia, which names him, was allowed to proceed in August 2025.

facts.claim: The 9/11 Commission's final report described Fahad al-Thumairy as an accredited diplomat at the Saudi consulate in Los Angeles from 1996 to 2003 and an imam at the King Fahad Mosque, employed by Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Islamic Affairs, and stated that after exploring the available leads it had not found evidence that he provided assistance to hijackers Nawaf al-Hazmi and Khalid al-Mihdhar.
facts.quote: After exploring the available leads, we have not found evidence that Thumairy provided assistance to the two operatives.

facts.claim: The 9/11 Commission reported that al-Thumairy met Omar al-Bayoumi at the Los Angeles consulate in February 2000, shortly before al-Bayoumi met the two hijackers at a restaurant; al-Thumairy denied knowing al-Bayoumi, although the two spoke by telephone numerous times, which al-Bayoumi said concerned religious matters.
facts.quote: Thumairy denied knowing al-Bayoumi, though the two talked on the phone numerous times

facts.quote: Al Thumairy was later denied entry into the United States in May 2003 after the State Department alleged that he might be involved in terrorist activity.

facts.claim: The first FBI document released under Executive Order 14040, a 16-page electronic communication dated April 4, 2016 summarizing Operation Encore, states, according to reporting on it, that al-Thumairy tasked an associate, whose name is redacted, to assist al-Hazmi and al-Mihdhar in Los Angeles, including taking them to the Mediterranean Gourmet Restaurant on Venice Boulevard. This is an FBI summary of interviews, not a finding of fact.
facts.quote: he tasked an associate with taking the two to the Mediterranean Gourmet Restaurant on Venice Boulevard — which was noted as a potential meeting place by the FBI

facts.claim: The FBI's Operation Encore closing material, released under Executive Order 14040, states that the evidence did not establish that al-Thumairy, al-Bayoumi and al-Jarrah knowingly conspired to assist the al Qaeda hijackers. None of the three was charged, and all have left the United States.
facts.quote: the evidence did not establish that Thumairy, Bayoumi, and Al-Jarrah knowingly conspired to assist the AQ hijackers in furtherance of the 9/11 attack.

facts.claim: On August 28, 2025, Judge George B. Daniels denied Saudi Arabia's renewed motion to dismiss the consolidated 9/11 families' claims, finding that the evidence supported a reasonable inference that al-Bayoumi's and al-Thumairy's employment was more than their official job titles suggested; the ruling allows the case to proceed and is not a finding of liability.
facts.quote: Saudi Arabia's explanations were "either self-contradictory or not strong enough to overcome the inference that" the Kingdom had employed two individuals, Omar al-Bayoumi and Fahad al-Thumairy, to assist the hijackers.

openQuestions: The connection to musaed-al-jarrah is a shared FBI casefile, not a stated relationship between the two men; the owner may prefer to drop it. The FBI release reported by Florida Bulldog says al-Jarrah directed al-Thumairy and al-Bayoumi, but this was not confirmed from the FBI document itself.
The 9/11 Commission's statement that al-Thumairy served at the consulate 1996-2003 comes from its notes (GPO-911REPORT-13.pdf); the owner should confirm the page before publishing.
